column1: # desktop/corpus/MANIFEST.tsv - every file fetch.sh will put in files/, with
# the provenance that makes it legal to use and the reason it is here.
# NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS COMMITTED AS AUDIO OR AS MIDI. fetch.sh downloads
# each row from the pinned commit and checks its sha256 against this table, in
# the same spirit as bench/README.md pinning Munt: the repository records what
# it read, not a copy of it.
# licence is what the SOURCE REPOSITORY states, read out of the file named in
# licence_file at the pinned commit -- not inferred from a project's reputation.
# Both licences here require the copyright notice to be kept with the work,
# which is why `copyright` is a column and not a footnote.
# columns, tab separated:
#   name        what ab.sh and scan.py call it
#   repo        github.com/<repo>
#   commit      pinned; the fetch URL contains it, so the bytes cannot drift
#   path        path inside that repo at that commit
#   bytes       measured here
#   sha256      measured here; fetch.sh refuses a mismatch
#   licence     SPDX identifier of the source repository's stated licence
#   licence_file    the file in that repo that states it
#   copyright   who holds it, and who wrote the piece
#   exercises   why this one is in the corpus and not another

column1: rolling
column9: (c) 2010-2021 OpenMSX Authors; "Keep on Rolling" by Trolley Trev (src/themes.list, README.md 6.0)
column10: the only file of 143 whose NOTE count alone reaches 32, the MT-32's partial ceiling, with no multiplier applied. Different idiom from Doom: jazz, not metal

column1: journey
column10: short and dense: 84 s at 48.3 note-ons/s, peak 24. The default when you want an A/B that finishes while you watch
